newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds tick up in light trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds tick up in light trading.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities climbed modestly higher in light trading on Friday, traders said.
In 30-year paper, discount coupons performed best, although FNMA and FHLMC premiums followed closely behind.
"Discounts are holding their own with the 10-year (Treasury note)," one trader said. "You could make a case that (spreads) widened a little bit overall, but really not much."
By late on Friday, mortgage-backeds generally were unchanged to 3/32 higher.

Specifically, GNMA 30-year 7.5-percent coupons were up 1/32 at 99-23/32, yielding 111 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable FNMA 30-years had risen 1/32 to 99-20/32, and FHLMCs were 1/32 higher at 99-26/32.
The 10-year note was up 3/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
On Friday morning the Commerce Department said the U.S. international trade gap shrank to $10.83 billion in August from a revised $11.60 billion the month before.
"I think most people were expecting a bigger fall in the deficit that what we got, said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A. Inc.
